newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China World Trade plans US$200 mln H shares.
newsitem.headline: China World Trade plans US$200 mln H shares.

text.p: Beijing-based China World Trade Centre Ltd plans to raise US$200 million in 1997 by issuing H shares, a company official said on Thursday.
H shares are mainland Chinese incorporated firms listed in Hong Kong.

The World Trade Centre, which leases and manages properties, plans to inject most of its assets into a new company to be listed in Hong Kong, the official told Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin. He added that the company has yet to be named.
The Hong Kong Stock Exchange has given the issue preliminary approval, he said, but he declined to give the pricing and precise timing of the offer.

The Centre is owned jointly by China Foreign Economic Trade Consulting Co under the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, and Kerry Industrial Co Ltd, a Hong Kong company. It is among 38 domestic firms approved by Beijing last December for listings abroad, the official said.

The firm plans to name JP Morgan and China Development Finance Co (H.K.) Ltd as main underwriters, the official said. Morgan Stanley and Credit Lyonnais Securities are also likely to be members of the underwriting group, he added.
The company plans to use the proceeds to build office and residential blocks in Beijing, the official said.

The company's main properties include the five-star China World Hotel and the four-star Traders Hotel, he said, adding the firm's total assets are valued at more than US$500 million and had net assets of US$430 million.
World Trade Centre Ltd racked up US$84 million in net profit in 1996, roughly the same as the 1995 level, the official said. The profit figure is not audited.
